createdBy: codex code review (T-008 round 4), filed by Claude
impact:
T-008 was the release gate that decided the locking primitive, and its answer was that BOTH candidates fail: a lock file must be reclaimed when its owner dies, and Node's syscalls cannot make that judgement safely. The failure is reproduced, not argued (spikes/locking/lock.race.test.mjs: two contenders both enter, both mint the same generation, and release() deletes a live successor's lock). The adopted design is a write-once port allocation published via link() plus a continuously held loopback listener.

Four downstream tickets still instruct implementers to build the rejected design. Anyone implementing them literally would rebuild the primitive the gate just disproved:

- T-010: publish path assumes pid/start-time/token lockfiles with inode revalidation before every publish and unlock. It also mandates generation/manifest fsync ordering, while the findings and spikes/locking/publish.mjs record a deliberate NO-fsync policy for derived snapshots (losing one costs a recomputation, not data). These are incompatible contracts, and the durability conflict needs an explicit decision either way rather than two documents disagreeing.
- T-011: repeatedly requires inode revalidation, a pid/start-time/token lockfile, and lockfile-replacement tests. Should be the write-once allocation plus a continuously held PortLock: unexpected-close loss witness, no PID record, no inode revalidation, domain-separated holder diagnosis that REFUSES startup on a foreign holder (never re-allocates), and no publication after observed loss.
- T-012: requires inode revalidation before every fast-tier publish and says publication rides T-010's fsync protocol. Should be PortLock.assertHeld()/observed-loss-discard semantics, and must be reconciled with whatever T-010's durability decision turns out to be.
- T-013: computation-lease scope requires expiry/takeover rules and per-namespace ownership records. The selected primitive has no reclaimable ownership record and no safe expiry takeover — exclusion lasts exactly while the kernel-held listener is bound, crash releases it automatically, and a live-but-hung holder can only justify bounded-wait-then-honest-stale. Implementing timeout-based reallocation would recreate the split-owner race the gate eliminated.

Also minor: T-014's description claims spikes/ contains only spikes/rounding, which T-008 made false. The intended point (no Swift helper prototype is committed) should be stated directly instead of via a repository inventory that will keep going stale.

Not fixed inline because it is outside T-008's scope — T-008's deliverable is docs/v0.2-prototype-findings.md, which now records the outcome, and T-008's own go/no-go wording has been amended to record candidate C. Rewriting four downstream tickets is a separate, deliberate act that should not ride along in a spike commit.
title: T-010/T-011/T-012/T-013 still specify the lockfile architecture T-008 rejected
